points.description: States the new steady-state error is zero (θss = θd), with the gravity cancellation shown or clearly asserted (the +mgℓ sinθ term cancels the gravity term, leaving Jθ̈ + (b+Kd)θ̇ + Kp(θ−θd) = 0).

levels.says: States zero error but gives no cancellation or reason.

points.description: Correct, justified statement about the poles. Accept any of: (a) the poles change in general because the gravity stiffness term mgℓ cosθ is removed from the characteristic equation (s² + ((b+Kd)/J)s + Kp/J instead of (Kp + mgℓ cosθss)/J); (b) at θd = 90° the gravity stiffness mgℓ cosθ is ~zero/negligible, so the poles are essentially unchanged at this operating point, though they would change elsewhere; (c) both together (best answer, no extra marks; note on script). Do not award an unjustified yes/no, or 'poles change because the plant is now linear' without identifying which coefficient (the mgℓ cosθ stiffness term) changes.

rubric.notes: Full marks: zero steady-state error with cancellation, plus a pole statement that names the mgℓ cosθ stiffness term (general answer, 90° answer, or both). Part marks only for zero error without justification. No marks for bare yes/no on poles. Note on the script candidates giving both answers.
